name: Vespid Dynamics Reconnaissance Beetle RB-2
description: A ground-based surveillance micro-drone the size and shape of a large beetle that navigates terrain autonomously, recording audio and video while being virtually indistinguishable from a real insect at casual observation. The RB-2 moves on six articulated legs that mimic insect locomotion, can climb walls, squeeze through gaps as small as 2 cm, and operates for 48 hours on a single charge. Its shell is colored and textured to match local insect populations, and it generates realistic insect movement patterns when stationary to avoid detection. The drone transmits compressed data bursts on a schedule to minimize RF signature.

specifications.info: insect profile; wall climbing capable; 200m range

story_hooks: A sweep of a sensitive facility found 14 RB-2 drones operating simultaneously in different rooms — someone has been running comprehensive ground-level surveillance for weeks.
An RB-2 was crushed by a target who noticed unusual insect behavior — the drone's data cache was intact and contained audio of conversations that implicate multiple corporate officers.

physical_description.visual_profile: A biomimetic surveillance micro-drone engineered to resemble a large beetle or cicada. The carapace is segmented and chitinous-looking, with an iridescent sheen that shifts between deep greens, burnt oranges, and metallic browns depending on angle and light. Six articulated legs fold and extend with uncanny organic precision. The head section houses a barely-visible lens cluster and minimal sensor array. At first glance, it reads as an oversized insect; closer inspection reveals precision engineering—hairline seams, micro-actuator joints, and barely-perceptible synthetic material beneath the organic camouflage layer.
physical_description.dimensions: 4 cm body length (approximately the size of a large stag beetle or carpenter ant); leg span extends to ~6 cm when fully articulated
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight handheld—under 15 grams; easily manipulated with tweezers or gentle fingers; pocketable in a protective case
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite exoskeleton with a bioengineered polymer carapace overlay; titanium-alloy leg joints; silicate-based sensor housing
physical_description.finish: Textured, semi-glossy carapace with realistic chitin-like ridging and segmentation; legs possess a matte finish with fine articulation lines; micro-abrasion texture prevents light reflection glare
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: graduated iridescent green-to-copper spectrum (mimics local Great Lakes region insect populations—cicadas and June beetles); accent: jet black segmentation lines and joint striping; translucent amber sensor dome at head
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimal external controls; micro-USB charging port (recessed, cap-protected) located on ventral thorax; status indicator LED (subdued amber, concealed beneath leg cavity); wireless data burst transmission only; all control via encrypted remote interface or autonomous pre-programming
distinctive_features: Six independently-articulated legs with joint mechanics that precisely mimic insect movement—each leg capable of microstepping for wall-adhesion climbing
Segmented carapace with realistic chitin texture that conceals HD camera lens behind transparent polymer 'eye' facet
Directional microphone port disguised as natural breathing aperture on left side
Micro-vibration generators beneath carapace produce realistic insect vibration patterns when stationary—legs twitch and antennae-analog sensors quiver to mimic resting behavior
Thermal signature dampening nano-coating reduces detectability to IR sensors
Barely-visible holographic etching of manufacturer serial on left rear leg joint (visible only under magnification)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS logo (minimalist wasp silhouette) laser-etched into ventral surface near power port; model designation 'RB-2' stamped in micro-font on starboard leg joint; regulatory compliance stamps (GLMZ Tier 2 certification, no-fly zone protocols) confined to service panel underside
physical_description.condition_typical: Fresh units display pristine synthetic carapace with perfect segmentation and high-gloss finish; units in field show subtle wear—micro-scarring on legs from terrain navigation, dust accumulation in joint crevices, occasional paint chips from wall-climbing. Battery-depleted units rest with legs partially contracted in a natural 'dormant insect' posture. Active units move in stop-start patterns, mimicking authentic insect locomotion with occasional directional reorientation and sensor-swiveling behavior.
